definitions.gloss: era, epoch, the beginning of an era
definitions.explanation: The starting point of a calendar system or historical era. Often refers to the beginning of the Common Era (A.D.) or the founding of a civilization.

definitions.gloss: A.D., the year (of the Common Era)
definitions.explanation: Used with year numbers to indicate dates in the Western calendar system. Often contrasted with {紀元前|きげんぜん} (B.C.).

examples.japanese: {紀元|きげん}{前後|ぜんご}の{歴史|れきし}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: Study history from around the beginning of the Common Era.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{皇紀|こうき}は{神武天皇|じんむてんのう}{即位|そくい}を{紀元|きげん}とする。
examples.english: Japan's imperial calendar takes the enthronement of Emperor Jimmu as its epoch.

examples.japanese: キリスト{教|きょう}の{暦|こよみ}では、イエスの{誕生|たんじょう}が{紀元|きげん}の{基準|きじゅん}になっている。
examples.english: In the Christian calendar, the birth of Jesus serves as the reference point for the era.

examples.japanese: {紀元|きげん}79{年|ねん}にポンペイが{滅|ほろ}びた。
ローマ{帝国|ていこく}は{紀元|きげん}476{年|ねん}に{滅亡|めつぼう}した。
examples.english: The Roman Empire fell in 476 A.D.

examples.japanese: この{遺跡|いせき}は{紀元|きげん}3{世紀|せいき}ごろのものと{推定|すいてい}されている。
examples.english: These ruins are estimated to date from around the 3rd century A.D.

notes:
USAGE:
{紀元|きげん} by itself typically refers to the Common Era (A.D.). To specify B.C., use {紀元前|きげんぜん}. In academic and historical writing, {紀元|きげん} may be abbreviated as {紀元|きげん}{後|ご} (A.D.) to contrast with {紀元前|きげんぜん} (B.C.).

HOMOPHONES:
Not to be confused with {期限|きげん} (deadline, time limit) or {機嫌|きげん} (mood, humor).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紀元前|きげんぜん}: B.C., before the Common Era
- {紀元後|きげんご}: A.D., after the Common Era
- {紀元|きげん}○{年|ねん}: year ○ A.D.
- {皇紀|こうき}: Japanese imperial era dating
